hints: Look closely at the energy levels in the diagram and notice whether the products finish higher or lower than the reactants.
Reaction 1 is acid-base neutralisation, which you should recall as a classic exothermic reaction with products lower in energy.
Check if reactions 2 and 3 both need continuous heating to break apart a stable compound, which points to the same endothermic profile.
walkthrough:
**Read the energy profile**

Look at the start and finish levels. The products are higher in energy than the reactants.

That means energy is taken in overall, so $\Delta H$ is positive:
$$\text{products higher than reactants = endothermic}$$

**Classify reaction 1**

Reaction 1 is neutralisation:
$$\text{NaOH} + \text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{NaCl} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
This forms water from $\text{H}^+$ and $\text{OH}^-$ and releases heat. It is exothermic, so products would be lower. It does NOT fit.

**Classify reactions 2 and 3**

Reaction 2 is thermal decomposition of limestone:
$$\text{CaCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{CaO} + \text{CO}_2$$
Reaction 3 is breaking down magnesium oxide:
$$2\text{MgO} \rightarrow 2\text{Mg} + \text{O}_2$$
Both break strong bonds in a stable compound and need continuous heating. Both are strongly endothermic, so both fit the profile with products higher than reactants.

**Conclude the match**

Only 2 and 3 show the endothermic profile with an activation energy hump. So the correct combination is 2 and 3 only.

options.A: Incorrect because it includes all three reactions. Reaction 1 is exothermic neutralisation, so its products would finish lower than reactants, the opposite of the diagram.
options.B: Incorrect because it includes reaction 1. Students sometimes forget neutralisation is exothermic and think all the listed reactions need heat, but NaOH + HCl releases heat.
options.C: Correct because both 2 and 3 are endothermic decompositions. CaCO3 decomposition and MgO decomposition both absorb energy, so products are at higher energy than reactants with an activation energy barrier, exactly as shown.
options.D: Incorrect because it includes only reaction 1 or excludes one of the endothermic reactions. Reaction 1 alone can never give a products-higher profile since neutralisation is exothermic.
